searchText: Yes, we had ethstats misconfigured. We fixed it yesterday. I have been thinking for a bit about removing block fields that are being deprecated by the Merge. I believe that `extra_data`, `mix_hash` and `nonce` could be removed without breaking smart contracts that read block header fields as they are last three fields of block structure for the moment, after London the last one will be `base_fee_per_gas` but it is exposed by the `BASEFEE` opcode. The `difficulty` field is right before the `number`, so, removing it is potentially breaking change for this kind of contracts. And if we consider removing those three fields then `difficulty` would be a perfect place for `randao`. cc <@!211091239112671234> <@!301186049323958275> `base_fee_per_gas` should still be present after The Merge. Oh, you mean that would be the last field in the header. * I do think we need a plan for removing fields from header. * I think we should set a very clear timeline on header shape changes and when they should be expected so people have ample time to migrate/adjust. * I generally like the idea of separating The Merge from The Cleanup, and would rather have a bit of bloat for some months between the two than trying to do too much at once in The Merge. Yeah, removing fields is not necessary happening at the time of the Merge. And I'd rather consider this for cleanups too. But if we have a decision on doing this kind of cleanup (even after the Merge) then we better take it in consideration for the `randao` EIP. So, `difficulty` might still be the best place for `randao`. Though, there is a complexity with this kind of replacement. ✅ <@!301186049323958275> <@!425572898787426305> is it really that much easier hardcoding the fields as opposed to dropping them? Could the difficulty of dropping (i.e. all the code this affects) described in the EIP-3675 or its magicians forum? Or rather the complexity comes from adding new fields (randao) after dropping the old ones could be hairy, and better to do that in one step? The worry with changing the header layout is that we don't know exactly what tools might break. Anything that does block validation has potential to break, which could be contracts validating merkle proofs, third party tools depending on merkle proofs, third party validating tools that aren't clients, etc. It essentially extends the scope of things we need to worry about. It is possible that it would be fine, but the cognitive overhead of determining that is likely high. Fair. I think this deserves its section in the rationale. I agree with that. cc <@425572898787426305> ☝️ Corresponding rationale section states the following (https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/a8dd00eeff5de6765084872ad30f45dcafcbcad9/EIPS/eip-3675.md#replacing-block-fields-with-constants): > Deprecated block fields are replaced with constant values to ensure the block format remains backwards compatible. Preserving the block format aids existing smart contracts and services in providing uninterrupted service during and after this transition. Isn't it kind of the same to what you have mentioned? <@!425279588009246720> <@!301186049323958275> It may be valuable to have like one sentence that mentions that tools/contracts that validate block proofs (which includes anything that validates transaction/state/receipt proofs from a blockhash) will likely need to be updated when we change the block layout. Just to make it a bit more clear that this is not the same as changing an API or something. High Goerli reorg count has nothing to do with 1559/London and everything to do with Clique. There is no leader node or leader elections (like the IBFT variants), so if the "in turn" block is too late all nodes that can should propose a next block, so seeing 4 reorgs at one block sounds like a clique network with 8 to 9 validators. <@552133098075193354> Aug 4 remains unchanged right? As I understand it, there only seems to be Erigon who would rather delay it, so I think we leave it as is unless other clients chime in today-ish? I will make sure to follow up with teams to get their thoughts. While troubleshooting a peering issue, I discovered a long lost project that attempted to add an Ethereum dissector to Wireshark. It is out of date and I had some trouble building it, so I didn't go much further. Informal poll of ACD - would having a wireshark dissector for RLPx/devp2p/ethereum be useful to enough teams to warrant me pursuing it? https://github.com/ConsenSys/ethereum-dissectors I would love to have it, would make eth version updates way easier + maybe peering issues on eth2 easier to debug This would have been useful during rayonism if it covers discv5, where we saw a bunch of p2p issues. It would certainly be valuable in the first testnets when execution is peered (it hasn't been tested as far as I know)

excerpts.author: marekm3498

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
I have been thinking for a bit about removing block fields that are being deprecated by the Merge. I believe that `extra_data`, `mix_hash` and `nonce` could be removed without breaking smart contracts that read block header fields as they are last three fields of block structure for the moment, after London the last one will be `base_fee_per_gas` but it is exposed by the `BASEFEE` opcode. The `difficulty` field is right before the `number`, so, removing it is potentially breaking change for this kind of contracts. 

And if we consider removing those three fields then `difficulty` would be a perfect place for `randao`.

cc <@!211091239112671234> <@!301186049323958275>

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: `base_fee_per_gas` should still be present after The Merge.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Oh, you mean that would be the last field in the header.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content:
* I do think we need a plan for removing fields from header.
* I think we should set a very clear timeline on header shape changes and when they should be expected so people have ample time to migrate/adjust.
* I generally like the idea of separating The Merge from The Cleanup, and would rather have a bit of bloat for some months between the two than trying to do too much at once in The Merge.

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content: Yeah, removing fields is not necessary happening at the time of the Merge. And I'd rather consider this for cleanups too. But if we have a decision on doing this kind of cleanup (even after the Merge) then we better take it in consideration for the `randao` EIP. So, `difficulty` might still be the best place for `randao`. Though, there is a complexity with this kind of replacement.

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content: <@!301186049323958275> <@!425572898787426305> is it really that much easier hardcoding the fields as opposed to dropping them? Could the difficulty of dropping (i.e. all the code this affects) described in the EIP-3675 or its magicians forum?

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content: Or rather the complexity comes from adding new fields (randao) after dropping the old ones could be hairy, and better to do that in one step?

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The worry with changing the header layout is that we don't know exactly what tools might break.  Anything that does block validation has potential to break, which could be contracts validating merkle proofs, third party tools depending on merkle proofs, third party validating tools that aren't clients, etc.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: It essentially extends the scope of things we need to worry about.  It is possible that it would be fine, but the cognitive overhead of determining that is likely high.

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content: Fair. I think this deserves its section in the rationale.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: I agree with that.  cc <@425572898787426305> ☝️

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
Corresponding rationale section states the following (https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/a8dd00eeff5de6765084872ad30f45dcafcbcad9/EIPS/eip-3675.md#replacing-block-fields-with-constants):
> Deprecated block fields are replaced with constant values to ensure the block format remains backwards compatible. Preserving the block format aids existing smart contracts and services in providing uninterrupted service during and after this transition.

Isn't it kind of the same to what you have mentioned? <@!425279588009246720>  <@!301186049323958275>

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: It may be valuable to have like one sentence that mentions that tools/contracts that validate block proofs (which includes anything that validates transaction/state/receipt proofs from a blockhash) will likely need to be updated when we change the block layout.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Just to make it a bit more clear that this is not the same as changing an API or something.

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: High Goerli reorg count has nothing to do with 1559/London and everything to do with Clique. There is no leader node or leader elections (like the IBFT variants), so if the "in turn" block is too late all nodes that can should propose a next block, so seeing 4 reorgs at one block sounds like a clique network with 8 to 9 validators.
